I have a mate who calls to me from the other side of the wood, and we share this place together. I am a tawny owl, and I have lived here all my life.

A brook. It runs through the meadow and under the oak. I drink from it when the moon is out. There is a lane, a road, and a lane with lights. I avoid the lights. The lane is where the jays and crows come. I hear them from the oak.

I drink in the hollow of the ash tree. The night is cool, and the dew is on the leaves. I sit still, and the dew runs down my feathers. I do not need much. I have the hollow, the leaves, and the silence. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I don't like it when the water is too loud, it makes me nervous. But I know it's safe, and the voles come out when the water is still. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I have never flown beyond the wood, but I hear the road at night, and the cars that pass. They are loud and dangerous. I do not like them.

Vole. The ones that run in the meadow at dusk. I hear them in the undergrowth, and I drop. They are quick, but I am quicker. I eat them whole, bones and all. The ones that come out at night are the best.

I hunt in the long grass for voles. They come out at dusk, scurrying through the undergrowth. I listen for their squeaks and rustles, then drop from the branch above. The grass is soft, so I land silently. Sometimes I catch one in my talons, sometimes it escapes. I eat the voles, and the rest I leave for the crows.

The oak is my castle, and the brook is my mirror. I have lived here for many years, and I do not leave it. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.
